implementation.currentAuthority: Node. The hosted Vercel entry calls identityHandler; the handler obtains a singleton identity runtime and performs root-auth, device authorization, Desktop token/refresh, server exchange, telemetry consent, account/device, and security-event operations through identity-db.
implementation.additionalStateOwner: The local Rudder server separately owns local-account exchange redemption and local auth-session persistence. Desktop owns client-side session/cookie installation and local telemetry/device state; it is not the hosted identity database writer.
implementation.rustEvidence: auth-core is a private Node/Rust actor-envelope protocol with verification and a process-local replay guard. Its module contract says it does not persist credentials, contact an identity provider, or write product state. It is not root account/session/device authority.
implementation.inactiveOrLegacyCode: identity/src/auth.ts defines a Better Auth factory, but no production callsite was found in the inspected tree. The identity HTTP E2E asserts /api/auth/sign-in/email is 404. The active hosted handler uses /api/root-auth and explicit Desktop/server paths. Local Rudder /api/auth/local-* routes are a separate Node implementation and do not make that Better Auth factory active.

private.status: Node-owned authenticated mutations and server-to-server operations.
private.details: The hosted handler validates account/device flows and uses identity-db state; consent synchronization is a separate authenticated collector hook. Local exchange/offline redemption and local-claim/signout require verified exchange, local session, or offline proof. Exact production secrets and deployed role grants were not read.

public.status: HTTP identity entry exists; live reachability not verified.
public.details: The Vercel adapter forwards requests to identityHandler. The handler exposes login/legal/health and auth/device/exchange endpoints. Source route presence does not prove current DNS, CDN, or deployment exposure.

default.status: Node handler and Node persistence are the active source default.
default.details: getIdentityRuntime selects the fixture adapter only for fixture environment; other environments select the Supabase root identity adapter. Desktop uses the first-party identity HTTP APIs and the local server exchange bridge. Supabase remains the upstream identity provider.

implementation.currentAuthority: Node standalone Express collector plus PostgreSQL. It verifies telemetry assertions/consent state, validates and persists event batches, updates installations/subjects, deduplicates by event ID and payload hash, and owns rollup/privacy aggregation, retention, deletion, and reporting behavior.
implementation.producerAndConsent: Desktop maintains local telemetry identity/consent state and schedules uploads when configured. Hosted Identity issues assertions and synchronizes consent through the private collector route. These producer/control paths remain Node/Electron.
implementation.storageAndMigrations: The deployed collector uses the rudder_analytics schema and role-separated collector, rollup, and reader connections. The deployment migration script applies 0140, 0141, and 0142 to that schema. Historical main-app migrations 0137 and 0139 create similarly named unqualified tables in the app database; they are not, by themselves, proof that the separate rudder_analytics deployment was migrated.
implementation.rustEvidence: No collector route, persistence, consent, rollup, or retention implementation was found in the bounded native/crates and native/bins source search. CLI MCP protocol helpers are unrelated.

private.status: Private data and control planes are explicit in source.
private.details: Ingest requires a signed identity assertion or configured anonymous authorization plus installation consent state. Internal consent/revoke hooks use deployment secrets. The report connection is distinct and read-only by role; maintenance uses a separate role and connection.

public.status: Compose publishes the collector on host loopback only; internet exposure is unknown.
public.details: The container listener binds 0.0.0.0, while the checked compose mapping is 127.0.0.1:hostPort:4318. No network overlay, reverse proxy, or live deployment was inspected.

default.status: Standalone deployment default, not a route mounted in the local Rudder API.
default.details: The collector has its own Node entrypoint and Docker Compose service, gated after migration completion. The local app route registration does not mount collector ingest. Desktop passes an optional collector URL and continues without upload if the scheduler cannot start.

implementation.currentAuthority: Node API routes, managed connection/binding/OAuth services, PostgreSQL state, and MCP SDK client transports. The runtime route handles initialize/discover/list/call and calls the configured external server over Streamable HTTP or STDIO.
implementation.state: Connection/OAuth state is stored in mcp_connections and related tables. Per-agent access is implemented through agent_custom_integration_bindings with connection_id linkage; do not treat the legacy table name as proof that bindings have already moved to a new table.
implementation.rustEvidence: cli-mcp-contract-core documents bounded primitives for a future Rust CLI/MCP binary and explicitly says it owns no authentication, product writes, or database state. It is not the managed remote MCP executor.

private.status: Organization- and run-scoped controls are implemented in Node.

public.status: Authenticated HTTP API surface; anonymous access is not evidenced.
public.details: Routes are registered under the Rudder API, including a bound MCP runtime endpoint. Deployment exposure and reverse-proxy reachability were not probed.

implementation.currentAuthority: Node. server/src/index.ts selects/reuses the local instance, initializes/starts it, applies startup migrations, checks post-migration invariants, and registers owned-process stop with the runtime supervisor. packages/db owns the provider and recovery routines. pnpm db:migrate uses a separate Node connection lifecycle and stops only an instance it started.
implementation.migrationBoundary: Node remains the migration writer: Drizzle applies SQL under advisory lock with recovery-point and post-migration gates. Rust migration-core validates assets; migration-history-postgres and migration-service read one repeatable-read snapshot; the migration-service source explicitly says it never locks, executes SQL, repairs history, or changes startup authority.
implementation.outsideServerAssets: CLI resolves/downloads the shared PostgreSQL payload and injects RUDDER_POSTGRES_BIN_DIR before importing the installed server. Desktop resolves/reconciles the shared payload, holds a lifecycle lock, and finalizes compatibility links after health. Dev scripts choose per-instance DB paths/ports. These assets are mandatory parts of a complete Rust lifecycle scope.
implementation.rustEvidence: Rust server-foundation provides service readiness with SELECT 1 and a foundation-only health receipt. It does not initialize or stop a PostgreSQL cluster. No Rust initdb/pg_ctl cluster lifecycle was found in the inspected crates/binaries.

private.status: Embedded listener is loopback-bound and storage is instance-scoped.
private.details: Provider start arguments bind 127.0.0.1. Per-instance config/data paths and runtime descriptors prevent the local provider from being treated as a shared public database. Existing local data was not opened or changed.

public.status: No public listener is evidenced for the embedded path.
public.details: DATABASE_URL selects an external PostgreSQL connection whose network exposure is owned by that provider and is outside the embedded process lifecycle.

default.status: When DATABASE_URL is unset, the Node server uses its embedded provider.
default.details: createLocalPostgresInstance selects verified official PostgreSQL 18.4 when RUDDER_POSTGRES_BIN_DIR is set; otherwise it loads the legacy embedded-postgres wrapper. Installed CLI runtime prepares/reuses the shared payload and sets the variable; Desktop has its own payload selection and lifecycle lock.

nextRustAuthoritySlice.recommended: Own the local server-exchange redemption transaction for POST /api/auth/local-exchange, leaving Identity provider verification and HTTP/cookie presentation behind a narrow Node adapter.
currentNodeTransaction: Verifies and validates issuer, audience, installation, expiry, subject, and verified email before entering the DB transaction.

Atomically inserts a one-time server_exchange_redemptions row, serializes issuer/subject binding creation with an advisory transaction lock, creates or refreshes the external user binding, creates the local user when needed, inserts the auth session, and links the redemption to that user.
explicitRetainedBoundaries: Supabase/upstream identity provider and hosted identity HTTP service
Offline grant, legacy installation claim, and signout-all until separately inventoried and accepted
acceptanceEdgesForThatSlice: Concurrent redemption of one jti has exactly one winner.
Issuer, audience, installation, expiry, and verified-email mismatches fail closed.
Concurrent first login for one issuer/subject creates one local binding.
Existing binding reuse and session persistence across server restart preserve current behavior.
Local-account upgrade E2E remains green on the exact Rust candidate.
blockers: Define a Rust bridge proof for verified exchange claims; auth-core actor envelopes are not identity-provider exchange claims.
Bind Rust transaction authority to existing Drizzle schema, legacy operator-state semantics, and activity/organization effects before choosing write ownership.
Real PostgreSQL concurrency and E2E acceptance are intentionally not run in this Phase0 evidence task.
